title: import preview: the client check flags a bad number but not an unknown picklist value, and the button still reads "Import 2 Rows" with a known-bad row
body:
**Filing gate ① — product defect with a named location and a reproduction.** reach: Tasks → Import a 2-row CSV where row 2 has Priority `Bogus` and Estimate `abc`.

**Who acts on it:** objectui triage → the console / records owner. ⛔ Not a claim. Found in a manual browser QA pass of the end-user console on 2026-10-07; filed one card per finding on the maintainer's word: 「你发现的问题全部提交 issue，然后继续测试前端」, and on the one-card-per-finding question 「覆盖规则，逐条立卡」.

## What happens

- The preview marks `abc` (number column) red, but not `Bogus`, although the client has the picklist's options.
- *Validate data* (server) reports only `Row 2: Priority: "Bogus" is not one of the allowed options` — the two checks each see half of the row's problems.
- With "1 row with errors" shown, the button still reads **Import 2 Rows**; the result is "1 created · 1 skipped" with the reason and *Download failed rows* (that part works well).

## Expected

The client marks unknown option values like other type errors; the button states what will happen ("Import 1 row, skip 1").

## Suggested direction (triage to rule)

Validate select/multiselect cells against the field options client-side (respecting *Keep unknown option values*), merge client and server findings into one per-row list, and count only importable rows on the button.

## Environment

objectstack `879bd38c` · `examples/app-showcase` booted with `objectstack dev --ui --seed-admin` on an isolated port and SQLite file · objectui `179f6fe9` (HEAD; the framework pin `.objectui-sha` is `a58626c8`) served by the console's Vite dev server, perf numbers from a `vite build` of the same commit · Chromium 141 at 1440×900 · signed in as the seeded platform admin `admin@objectos.ai` unless stated.

- No hit describes this defect.
- Positive control in the same run: *related lists action id refusal notice shown to end users* on objectstack-ai/objectui returned objectstack-ai/objectui#11768: yes.
